span.p: First principles: why nothing beat SPARC

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
1 target is low-rank in the constraint dimension
only SPARC projects onto it explicitly

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
2 identity causes magnitude (hypothesis)
binding is the event; μ is downstream
not isolated by the WOMu ablation

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
3 AQL and Winkler are different functionals
middle vs band edges

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
4 conformal equalizes coverage
so the contest is width-at-coverage

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
5 width/coverage coupling is a law here
routing proved it: coverage collapsed to 73.1%

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Decision tree
PRIMARY: calibration + coherence + efficiency + OOD
SAFE FLOOR: calibration + parity + efficiency
BEAT-EVERYTHING: tested as Godmode, failed
FORBIDDEN: hide LQR / compare only to weak baselines

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Honest limitations
no method is PIT-uniform
AQL and CRPS are parity, not superiority
cross-year error edge does not hold
seasonal 3-window claim not in the canonical build
one market, one year, one headline pair
scope: central 90% band; extreme tail events out of scope

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: D7 - The God model (10 experiments)

span.p:
The idea
every model wins exactly one axis
linear wins average error, persistence wins MAE
physics rule is a free prior; monotone head rescues coherence
conformal guarantees coverage
so fuse the winners into one model

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The fusion design
linear spine + attention residual + physics bias
+ monotone head + conformal
scored on calibrated Winkler, not AQL

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Verdict: NEGATIVE
10 tested directions, none beats SPARC
(24 h, 5-seed; SPARC soft 18.20 / hard 18.00)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
1 linear spine + market prior + conformal
cal-Winkler 20.14, cov 90.50 FAIL (vs LQR 20.03)
sharp but loses the calibration

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
2 time inside the attention query
cal-Winkler 18.38 vs SPARC 18.20 FAIL
fixing the architecture did not improve calibration

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
3 identity-only, drop μ magnitude
cal-Winkler 18.06 (best probe) but fails its AQL-parity line
simpler is nearly as good, no gain

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
4 full additive fusion
cal-Winkler 18.26 FAIL
complexity without a calibration gain

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
5 train on the metric you report (Move D)
cal-Winkler 18.34 but coverage 87.9 - under-covers FAIL

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
6 feature-adaptive conformal (CQR, Move E)
cal-Winkler 17.38, width 12.14, but coverage 85.3 - invalid FAIL

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
7 level/spread factorization (MV)
cal-Winkler 18.16 vs 18.20, p=0.88 FAIL (wash)

span.p:
8 nested normalized conformal (β)
normalized PIT worse (KS 5e-28 vs 5.6e-12) RULE OUT

span.p:
9 pointwise min-width routing (γ)
selected coverage 73.13% RULE OUT
min-selection destroys marginal coverage

span.p:
10 tune the crossing penalty (λ)
cal-Winkler 18.08 vs 18.20, p=0.41 FAIL (n.s.)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Other paper's rule and head (canonical conformal)
market-rule-embedded 18.17, hier 18.11 (24 h)
SPARC family within 0.2: soft 18.20, hard 18.00 (n.s.)
hard head on SPARC 18.00 vs soft 18.20 - comparable

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: D6 - Generalization

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
What 3 pairs means exactly
1 primary HB_HUBAVG to HB_PAN: full comparison, 5 seeds
2 probes: HB_NORTH 93.87%, HB_WEST 93.85%: proposed model only
claim = calibration consistency, not a ranked comparison on 3

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Probe AQL caution
NORTH AQL 0.51, WEST 0.81 are LOWER than primary 1.25
but AQL is in $/MWh and scale-dependent: those pairs have smaller spreads
baselines were not run there → no error win claim

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Near-range OOD (canonical monthly Jan-May 2026, 5-seed)
SPARC coverage 87.7% vs LQR 88.1%; SPARC Winkler 27.86 vs 30.74
electricity is strongly seasonal; which corridors bind changes with the season
so season-to-season is the decision-relevant test
NOTE: the 3-window 87.8/92.7/62.5 numbers are NOT in the canonical build

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Cross-year full 2025→2026 (5-seed): stress limit
SPARC coverage 90.1% vs LQR 81.4%; calendar 90.5% vs 82.3%
8,978 params → retrain frequently
train-once-generalize-a-year is the wrong question

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Conformal defense — the result
wrap LQR in flat split-conformal → coverage 91.82%, width 12.71
but calibrated Winkler 20.03, still worse than SPARC 18.20
→ conformal equalizes coverage but not width-efficiency
→ the edge is INTRINSIC to the architecture

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Sensitivity (5-seed) - now varies
leads 1/2/4/12/24 h → Winkler 18.43 → 19.74 → 20.38 → 21.16 → 20.25
calibration degrades as the snapshot ages; 24 h beats 4/12 h (diurnal alignment)

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: D5 - Protocol, findings, mechanism (canonical 5-seed)

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Protocol
CPU, chronological 70-15-15
5 seeds 42-46, 7 quantiles
AQL = pure pinball; penalty training-only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Why 5 seeds
one run can be lucky
5 seeds give mean ± std and paired tests
a single-seed win is never a claim

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
What an ablation is
remove ONE component, retrain, measure the drop
isolates that component's contribution

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Field
SPARC + 8 baselines + 6 ablations

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Raw results, primary pair
SPARC coverage 89.41, Winkler 20.25, AQL 1.254, AQCR 0.11
LQR 73.13, 24.43, 1.171, 31.99
MLP 87.37, 23.34, 1.404
LSTM 74.20, Transformer 76.67, XGB 79.34, RF 32.19

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Findings
1 best calibrated (cal-Winkler 18.20 soft / 18.00 hard)
2 LQR now significantly better on AQL (p=0.015); beats deep nets
3 best coherence vs linear/trees (0.11% vs 32.0%/15.1%/62.2%)
4 7-9x more efficient (8,978 params)
5 coverage significant vs LQR (t=8.33, p=0.0011); vs MLP n.s.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Calibrated (flat split-conformal)
SPARC cov 91.90, width 13.90, Winkler 18.20 (soft; hard 18.00)
LQR cov 91.82, width 12.71, Winkler 20.03
MLP cov 94.27, width 17.78, Winkler 20.61
= coverage equalized; SPARC wins width-efficiency

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Honest negatives
LQR wins raw AQL (1.171 vs 1.254, p=0.015)
CRPS parity (1.910 vs 2.074)
one ablation (no path embed, AQL 1.191) edges us
scope: central 90% band, extreme events out of scope

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Ablations (raw coverage)
Uniform attention: 89.41 → 77.48 (-11.93pp), AQL 1.254 → 1.225
= attention is the load-bearing calibration mechanism
No constraint-ID feature -4.71pp; zeroed path embedding (constant query) -7.11pp
No temporal vector (incl. lags): AQL 1.682 = temporal drives point error
Explicit energy term added ≈ full (88.64) = energy cancels in the spread
WOMu (readout fixed to 1, no constraint info): -1.09pp = interpretation open

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Mechanism evidence
attention 0.23-0.26 (mean 0.25) on top-3 μ slots
about 12x the uniform 0.020
highest 0.260 in the top bin (mean max μ 59.3)

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: D4 - Metrics

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Running example
Observed value: y = 10
90% interval: [L, U] = [-5, 15]
Median forecast: q_0.5 = 8

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
AQL / pinball loss
ρ_τ(y - q_τ) = (y - q_τ) · (τ - I[y < q_τ])
At τ = 0.5: error 2 → loss 1.0
At τ = 0.9: error 2 → loss 1.8
standard quantile loss; the anchor's headline

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Empirical interval coverage
Coverage = (1/N) · Σ_t I[L_t ≤ y_t ≤ U_t]
For a 90% interval: L_t = q_0.1 and U_t = q_0.9
88 of 100 hours inside = 88%
THE decision metric: a desk sizes from the band

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Winkler score for a 90% interval
W = U - L, if L ≤ y ≤ U
W = U - L + 20(L - y), if y < L
W = U - L + 20(y - U), if y > U
rewards covering AND narrow; cannot be gamed with a wide box

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Adjacent quantile crossing rate
AQCR = crossings / adjacent quantile pairs
A crossing occurs when q_τ,j > q_τ,j+1
SPARC 0.11% vs LQR 31.99%

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
THE METRIC-PARADOX
AQL is middle-dominated → LQR wins it
Winkler taxes the band edges → SPARC wins it
the reported winner is an artifact of the metric

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Why calibration matters for trading
a band claiming 90% but holding 73%
leaves 27% of hours under-hedged
losses live in the missed hours, not the mean error
low mean error does NOT rescue bad intervals

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No tail contradiction
Winkler tails = the 0.10 and 0.90 edges of the NORMAL band
spike hours = top 5% EXTREME events, far beyond 0.90
different things; extreme events are OUT OF SCOPE here

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
CRPS
proper score on the whole predictive CDF
rewards calibration + sharpness

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
PIT / KS
actual 10, forecast CDF 0.5 → PIT 0.5
uniform = calibrated; U-shape = too narrow; cap = too wide
EVERY method fails uniformity → comparative claim only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Efficiency
8,978 params vs MLP 64,456 / Transformer 78,536
enables frequent retraining

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Significance
5 seeds → paired t / Wilcoxon / sign
coverage vs LQR: t = 8.33, p = 0.0011

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Concrete quantile example
point: spread = 8 dollars, hides the risk
quantiles: median 8, 90% band [-5, 15]
if spread realizes 30, the point forecast was useless
0.90 tells you the worst plausible case
weather analogy: 25C vs 18-27C with 90% chance
0.10 and 0.90 = the band a desk sizes from

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: D3 - The model

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Inputs
top-50 constraint slots, 4 numbers each
(μ, constraint ID, kV level, flow ratio)
temporal vector: 6 Fourier terms + 3 lagged spreads (18-d)
path embedding

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Slot encoder
one shared layer per slot (Linear 4→8 + ReLU)
empty slots are zeros → always 50 slots
the constraint ID is one of the 4 input numbers

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Keys and values
keys = the encoded slots
each value → one number μ̃_k
(learned congestion signal of that constraint)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Constraint attention
a_k = exp(score_k) / Σ_j exp(score_j)
Σ_k a_k = 1
a_k = learned relative exposure weight
(plays the role of ΔSF: positive + normalized,
so it captures relative magnitude; sign and scale
are absorbed downstream)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Temporal encoder
Fourier terms + lagged spreads
joins in the head, NOT in the attention

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Quantile head
[path embedding, temporal vector, attention output]
→ MLP (128) → 7 quantiles
soft head + crossing penalty, no sorting
raw AQCR 0.11% vs LQR 32.0%, MLP 15.1%
(hard head 0.00% by construction)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Query = the path embedding only
asks which constraints matter for this pair

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Weighted blend of the value signals
= Σ_k a_k · μ̃_k
same form as Σ_k ΔSF_k · μ_k

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Training loss
L = Σ_t Σ_τ ρ_τ(y_t - q_hat_τ,t) + λ · crossing penalty
ρ_τ(u) = u · (τ - I[u < 0])
penalty is training-only, never a metric

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hard (hierarchical) head tested on SPARC
calibrated Winkler 18.00 (hard) vs 18.20 (soft) → comparable; kept soft as flagship

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Lagged spreads t-24 / t-48 / t-168
part of the temporal vector
no separate encoder

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Why attention, not something else?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Raw concatenation of the constraints
REJECTED
the number of binding constraints changes every hour
the network needs a fixed-size input

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Mean-pool everything
REJECTED
treats every binding line as equally important for every path
destroys selectivity: a line near the sink should matter more than one far away

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
MLP over the constraint features
REJECTED
no explicit weight per constraint
cannot tell you which line drove the forecast

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
RNN or Transformer over the constraint set
REJECTED
a set has no order; first and last are interchangeable
imposes an order that does not exist

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ATTENTION — CHOSEN
handles a variable-size set
gives a per-path weight to each constraint
order-free (permutation-invariant)
the weights play the role of learned ΔSF
→ interpretable by construction

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Why 50 fixed slots
K varies each hour → pad to 50 with zeros
fixed-size input; attention then picks what matters

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
What others do, and why it is wrong for this problem
feed the price as a time series, never see the constraint set
= model the shadow, not the cause

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: D2 - SCED, the anchor, our move

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
SCED optimization
solved every hour

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Outputs simultaneously
LMPs, binding constraints, shadow prices

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
LMP identity is EXACT at the optimum
LMP_i = λ + Σ_k SF_k,i · μ_k
λ, SF, μ are the primal and dual
quantities of the optimization

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
But they are ENDOGENOUS
defined only by solving the clearing
no closed-form function from raw inputs

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Computing them means re-solving SCED
a large complementarity problem,
not a differentiable layer

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ΔSF is not published for each
source-destination pair
depends on topology + operating point

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Rule is real, but NOT transcribable
so LEARN the exposure weights

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Anchor: Yu et al., Austria
MRINN

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Known piecewise settlement formula
embedded as differentiable layers
= RULE-EMBEDDING

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hard hierarchical head
non-crossing by construction, AQCR = 0

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Never reports coverage, Winkler, CRPS, PIT

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Our move: condition on the PAST published clearing outputs
previous day's clearing (t-24 h, ADR-0013) - the freshest snapshot available at bid time
the target hour's own μ is NOT used —
it exists only after that hour clears, so using it would leak

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
What is given: the lagged μ (a published output)
What is learned: ΔSF, as attention weights

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
SPARC is constraint-aware
NOT market-rule-informed

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Which rule do we embed? NONE
the identity is used as structure

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Q: couldn't you differentiate through SCED?
In principle yes, but it needs a full, maintainable
ERCOT SCED model with complementarity — a different,
much larger program. The clearing outputs are already published.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: D1 - Market, shadow price, spread

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: ERCOT day-ahead, nodal

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Nodal price
LMP_i = λ + Σ_k SF_k,i · μ_k

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Energy component λ
same at every node

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Congestion component
Σ_k SF · μ, location-specific

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Shadow price μ_k
μ_k = marginal cost of relaxing
constraint k by 1 MW

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Example: road at capacity
one more MW costs +$20
therefore μ = $20/MWh

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Selection: per hour, per constraint
sort by its own μ descending, take top 50
binding only, snapshot lagged 24 h (previous day's clearing)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Path spread
ΔLMP_s→d = LMP_d - LMP_s
= Σ_k (SF_k,d - SF_k,s) · μ_k
= Σ_k ΔSF_k · μ_k
(code target = src − snk = HB_HUBAVG − HB_PAN,
i.e. the same quantity with the opposite sign)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
λ cancels exactly
spread = pure congestion differential

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Differential shift factor
ΔSF_k = SF_k,d - SF_k,s
Example: 0.6 - 0.1 = 0.5
If μ_k = $20/MWh, contribution = $10/MWh

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
If ΔSF_k = 0, the constraint affects both ends equally
Contribution to the spread = 0

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT ASSUMPTION
μ is the market's own signal of
where and how badly the grid is constrained

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Needs domain understanding,
not just sending prices to ML. And that is shown by our results

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
